name: email-constraint-leading-at-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is '@example.com' (a stray leading '@' with no localpart). RFC 5280 4.2.1.10 spells out three valid encodings — a complete mailbox 'user@example.com', a bare hostname 'example.com', or a leading-dot domain '.example.com'. The '@example.com' form is not in that list and has historically been interpreted by OpenSSL as equivalent to the bare 'example.com' form. The leaf SAN 'foo@example.com' is at the host example.com; per RFC the constraint is malformed and the chain must be rejected.
references: BoringSSL 9708047e — crypto/x509: remove OpenSSL exception for name constraints '@example.com'
notes: Probes the OpenSSL legacy exception that treats a constraint of '@example.com' as the all-mailboxes-at form. BoringSSL/AWS-LC explicitly removed this exception in Apr 2026 and now reject the constraint as UNSUPPORTED_NAME_SYNTAX; OpenSSL and LibreSSL still accept it, which means a sub-CA constrained with the malformed form is treated as binding by some validators and as a no-op by others.
